business_problem: Using AWS IoT Core and other AWS services, Visteon can help automakers provide value for customers and address their own challenges.
solution_summary: As drivers increasingly expect their cars to connect seamlessly with their digital lives, Visteon is redefining how it builds cockpit electronics for automakers. “Visteon applies the smartphone experience to how users interact with their cars.” To develop its connected vehicle innovations, Visteon builds its suite of solutions—called AllGo—on top of Amazon Web Services (AWS). AllGo uses AWS services for storage, compute, Internet of Things (IoT) functionality, and vehicle connectivity. The ECUs use software, graphics processors, and CPUs powered by Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2), which provides secure and resizable compute capacity for virtually any workload.

solution_components.name: AWS IoT Core
solution_components.role: Connects IoT devices securely to cloud ingestion and device-management services.

solution_components.name: Amazon EC2
solution_components.role: Provides elastic compute capacity for application, analytics, and infrastructure workloads.

solution_components.name: Amazon S3
solution_components.role: Stores datasets, objects, model artifacts, or binary assets at scale.

solution_components.name: AWS IoT Device Management
solution_components.role: Registers, groups, and remotely manages fleets of connected devices.

solution_components.name: Amazon Kinesis
solution_components.role: Streams and processes high-volume event and telemetry data in real time.

data_flow: In 2022, Visteon unveiled plans for its AllGo App Store, which features preloaded popular apps for navigation, parking, infotainment, and other functions.
business_outcome: “Our productivity increases, and we deliver innovative products faster.” Alongside AWS solutions architects and technical account managers, Visteon operates in line with the AWS Well-Architected Framework , which describes key concepts, design principles, and architectural best practices for designing and running workloads in the cloud.
architecture_clues: For the OTA update feature, Visteon assigns a unique identity to each vehicle using AWS IoT Core’s device registry .
Using AWS IoT Device Management —which helps register, organize, monitor, and remotely manage IoT devices at scale—Visteon groups devices to receive automatic updates according to specific criteria.

The automaker sets the speed of deployment as well as campaign start and end dates using Jobs , a feature of AWS IoT Device Management, which defines a set of remote operations that can be sent to and run on one or more devices connected to AWS IoT Core.
“We can point to every vehicle that’s available with the automaker and monitor the state of each campaign and every detail seamlessly in the cloud,” Balakrishnan says.
evidence_quotes: Based in Michigan, Visteon provides in-vehicle technology to automakers around the globe, helping them bring digital products to drivers quickly without it requiring millions of dollars in development costs.

Since introducing the industry’s first on-board domain controller in 2018, Visteon has experienced exponential growth—with the third quarter of 2023 marking 18 consecutive quarters in which it has outperformed the market.
The domain controller, Visteon SmartCore, consolidates a vehicle’s electronic control units (ECUs).
The ECUs use software, graphics processors, and CPUs powered by Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2), which provides secure and resizable compute capacity for virtually any workload.

To securely connect vehicles to the cloud, Visteon uses AWS IoT Core , which lets companies connect billions of IoT devices and route trillions of messages to AWS services without managing infrastructure.
